analysis: Examined base_text units 58 and 59 of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 46536-48178). The unit content is public synthetic test-vector data: repeated filler text, token ID arrays, and fixed plan hashes. It contains no secrets, credentials, keys, or real consumer data (A-001 content is explicitly 'Public followup' and 'Public synthetic cache-parity input'). The file_changes patch excerpt (truncated) shows head-side edits at other ranges: adding additional_context enable_thinking=false to template_input, and altering prompt_token_count, chain_hash block boundaries and token_ids. The ranges within these units (base 46536-48178) overlap none of the listed changed base ranges, since those are at roughly 3024-4824, 43813-45533, and 52418-54138. Hence these units are unchanged context only. The changed vectors affect prompt-contract/prefix-cache chain hashes (T-041 cache-parity vectors) but are a test fixture, not executable code; no authorization, attestation, encryption or trust-boundary behavior (TB-002, TB-011) is modified. Integration questions: whether the Swift provider and Go coordinator implementations that consume these vectors were updated consistently (the template_input additional_context change and the changed chain hashes and prompt_contract_id must match both sides). A mismatch would cause cache-key or prompt-contract divergence, which is a correctness/availability risk and not a demonstrable security regression from the supplied evidence. Truncated patch excerpt and the head text for changed ranges were not supplied in these units, so the full effect of the changes cannot be assessed here.
